realProviderResults.reason: Not run: the deployment hold and paused manual testing (28 Oct). A real run would spend from the shared money and search limits (/day, 0/month; 10/100 public searches), which stay unchanged. When allowed, run each question once and report each run on its own, not as a benchmark.

whatThisProves: What the code refuses or keeps for each case, whatever the model proposes. It does not measure how often a real model proposes the wrong reply, or the quality of real search results.
knownLimits: Conflicting official pages: only amounts are compared, for the same capitalised subject, across pages that were read. Disagreements in words (rules, dates, eligibility) are not detected. The explanation check looks for words such as "differ" or "conflict" (English, Arabic, French), not for a good explanation.

Scope comes from listed hosts, a short list of UK-wide gov.uk paths (immigration, passports, national taxes) and the page’s own words ("In England", "across the UK"). Anything else is unknown. The UK-wide path list is incomplete, so some genuinely UK-wide pages will be treated as unknown and need a qualified answer.

Unknown scope must be qualified in the reply, with or without a location. The qualifier check is pattern-based ("doesn’t say whether it applies", "may not apply", in English, Arabic and French): it confirms a qualification is present, not that it is accurate.

A page tied to another place is accepted at country level when the person gave no place; once a place is known or named, it must say whose rule it is. A sentence that names the page’s place passes even if that rule is irrelevant to the person.
Where the person is comes from residence phrases, the profile city, or a single place named. A council page counts when the person named that council’s place; council boundaries are not checked.
Scripted model: these cases show what the code refuses or keeps, not how often a real model proposes the wrong reply. 0 real-provider runs.
